headline: Wheaton (Mass.) leads NEWMAC in scoring and defense
dek: Wheaton (Mass.) lost just three times in a season built on eleven wins and seven draws across all matches. Scoring 38 goals while conceding seventeen gave the program the sharpest margin in the NEWMAC, even as Babson finished unbeaten atop the conference table.

pattern.label: derived
pattern.text: Scoring separates the NEWMAC into sharp tiers: Wheaton (Mass.) produced 38 goals across all matches, more than WPI and Clark combined.

wire.line: NEWMAC sides won 35 non-conference matches against 28 defeats and 21 draws, scoring 132 goals and conceding 108.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Two matches past their scheduled dates carry no published result, and both involve Coast Guard: against Roger Williams and at Johnson & Wales.

findings.label: derived
findings.text: MIT spread its 36 goals across at least sixteen different scorers, distributing its attack across the roster.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Emerson defender Carlo Carson scored eight goals on 50 shots, matching the highest goal total in the conference from the back line.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Salve Regina goalkeeper Adonis Santiago made 63 saves and posted a 0.818 save percentage, allowing fourteen goals all season.

last_match.line: Babson finished conference play unbeaten and took its only defeats against non-conference opponents.

validation.policy: observed and derived claims are recomputed against the data home before publish; failures are dropped, not softened. signal and projected pass on schema unless the data contradicts a figure. context is never validated as a finding.
